text: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
The grass is always greener on the other side of the fence.
You can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink.
When life gives you lemons, make lemonade.
A picture is worth a thousand words.
If at first you don't succeed, try, try again.
Don't put all your eggs in one basket.
People who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones.
Birds of a feather flock together.
You can't judge a book by its cover.
Absence makes the heart grow fonder.
Good things come to those who wait.
An apple a day keeps the doctor away.
The early bird catches the worm, but the second mouse gets the cheese.
Keep your friends close and your enemies closer.
You can't have your cake and eat it too.
Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me.
The best things in life are free.
Every cloud has a silver lining.
Don't bite the hand that feeds you.
The pen is mightier than the sword.
A penny saved is a penny earned.
Too many cooks spoil the broth.
Remember, Rome wasn't built in a day.
All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy.
If a job is worth doing, it is worth doing well.
A job well begun is half done.
A bad workman always blames his tools.
Always strike while the iron is hot.
Never put off till tomorrow what you can do today.
Elbow grease is the best polish.
Hard work never did anyone any harm.
Don't cross the bridge until you come to it.
Always measure twice and cut once.
Slow and steady wins the race.
Where there's a will, there's a way.
The squeaky wheel gets the grease.
A chain is only as strong as its weakest link.
Two heads are better than one.
Jack of all trades, master of none.
You must learn to walk before you run.
If you want something done right, do it yourself.
Don't bite off more than you can chew.
Plan your work and work your plan.
Always put business before pleasure.
All things are difficult before they are easy.
You only get out what you put in.
A good beginning makes a good ending.
Necessity is the mother of invention.
Little by little does the trick.
Constant dropping wears away the stone.
Keep your nose to the grindstone.
You should practice what you preach.
Great talkers are little doers.
The devil finds work for idle hands to do.
Money doesn't grow on trees, you know.
A fool and his money are soon parted.
Take care of the pennies and the pounds will take care of themselves.
Cut your coat according to your cloth.
Don't spend what you don't have.
Money can't buy you happiness.
In the end, you get what you pay for.
Don't be penny wise and pound foolish.
If you buy cheap, you buy twice.
He who pays the piper calls the tune.
Don't throw good money after bad.
Money is a good servant but a bad master.
You should always live within your means.
A light purse is a heavy curse.
You can't take it with you when you go.
Time and tide wait for no man.
All good things must come to an end.
Time flies when you're having fun.
There's no time like the present.
Haste makes waste, so take your time.
The more haste, the less speed.
Just take it one day at a time.
Better an hour too early than a minute too late.
There is a time and a place for everything.
You can't turn back the clock.
Better late than never, but better never late.
You are never too old to learn.
Experience is the best teacher.
Two wrongs don't make a right.
Ask no questions and hear no lies.
It's better to be safe than sorry.
There's no fool like an old fool.
A wise man changes his mind; a fool never does.
Hindsight is always twenty-twenty.
A problem shared is a problem halved.
You learn something new every day.
Wise men learn by other men's mistakes; fools by their own.
The wise man does at once what the fool does at last.
Ask a silly question and you get a silly answer.
There is no royal road to learning.
It's easy to be wise after the event.
A word to the wise is sufficient.
Believe nothing of what you hear and only half of what you see.
A fool may ask more questions in an hour than a wise man can answer in seven years.
What you don't know can't hurt you.
Better to ask the way than go astray.
You should always look before you leap.
To be forewarned is to be forearmed.
Hope for the best, but prepare for the worst.
Don't burn your bridges behind you.
Better the devil you know than the devil you don't.
If it ain't broke, don't fix it.
It's best to leave well enough alone.
It is better to bend than to break.
Don't trouble trouble until trouble troubles you.
Never judge a man until you have walked a mile in his shoes.
Don't make a mountain out of a molehill.
Don't wash your dirty linen in public.
Better to have it and not need it than need it and not have it.
Better to light a candle than to curse the darkness.
Honesty is always the best policy.
The truth will always come out in the end.
Cheaters never win and winners never cheat.
A lie has no legs to stand on.
An honest man's word is as good as his bond.
Tell the truth and shame the devil.
A liar should have a good memory.
A clear conscience is a soft pillow.
Say what you mean and mean what you say.
Give credit where credit is due.
Never promise more than you can perform.
A man is only as good as his word.
Speech is silver, but silence is golden.
Empty vessels make the most noise.
Always think before you speak.
The least said, the soonest mended.
Sticks and stones may break my bones, but words will never hurt me.
A word spoken is past recalling.
If you can't say anything nice, don't say anything at all.
It's not what you say, it's how you say it.
Keep your mouth shut and your eyes open.
Many a true word is spoken in jest.
That is easier said than done.
Don't tell tales out of school.
Hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil.
A still tongue makes a wise head.
It's not what you know but who you know.
Self-praise is no recommendation.
The bigger they are, the harder they fall.
Don't get too big for your boots.
Don't let success go to your head.
Even a stopped clock is right twice a day.
You win some and you lose some.
It's not whether you win or lose, it's how you play the game.
Failure is the mother of success.
You should never rest on your laurels.
A winner never quits and a quitter never wins.
Nothing is impossible to a willing heart.
He who laughs last laughs longest.
You should quit while you're ahead.
Fall seven times, stand up eight.
Whatever goes up must come down.
Better to have tried and failed than never to have tried at all.
When the going gets tough, the tough get going.
It's a long road that has no turning.
Never give up and never give in.
When one door closes, another opens.
There's light at the end of the tunnel.
If you can't beat them, join them.
There is no gain without pain.
Where there is life, there is hope.
It is better to wear out than to rust out.
Make the most of what you have.
When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
It's first come, first served.
One man's loss is another man's gain.
Make the best of a bad situation.
You have to take the rough with the smooth.
All that glitters is not gold.
Beauty is in the eye of the beholder.
Appearances are often deceiving.
The clothes do not make the man.
Handsome is that handsome does.
A man is judged by his deeds, not his words.
First impressions are the most lasting.
Things are not always what they seem.
Every man is innocent until proven guilty.
The exception proves the rule.
There are two sides to every story.
Six of one and half a dozen of the other.
It takes all sorts to make a world.
There's no accounting for taste.
It is the thought that counts.
What goes around comes around in the end.
One good turn deserves another.
You can't please everyone all the time.
One man's trash is another man's treasure.
There is no smoke without fire.
Love makes the world go round.
Marry in haste, repent at leisure.
Faint heart never won fair lady.
A good wife makes a good husband.
The way to a man's heart is through his stomach.
Never go to bed on an argument.
Love and a cough cannot be hid.
Lucky at cards, unlucky in love.
Love me little and love me long.
Lovers' quarrels are soon mended.
Faults are thick where love is thin.
The heart that loves is always young.
The falling out of lovers is the renewing of love.
Love is sweet, but tastes best with bread.
A deaf husband and a blind wife are always a happy couple.
Marry your son when you will, your daughter when you can.
Happy is the bride the sun shines on.
Something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue.
There are plenty more fish in the sea.
There's many a good tune played on an old fiddle.
A friend to all is a friend to none.
Make new friends, but keep the old; one is silver, the other gold.
Love your neighbour, but don't pull down the fence.
A hedge between keeps friendship green.
Two is company, three is a crowd.
The more, the merrier; the fewer, the better fare.
A good neighbour is better than a distant friend.
Old friends and old wine are best.
The best mirror is an old friend.
A friend's frown is better than a fool's smile.
Before you make a friend, eat a bushel of salt with him.
Better to be alone than in bad company.
A man is known by the company he keeps.
Tell me who your friends are and I'll tell you who you are.
A fair-weather friend changes with the wind.
You can choose your friends but not your family.
The apple doesn't fall far from the tree.
Like mother, like daughter; like father, like son.
Children should be seen and not heard.
Little pitchers have big ears.
It takes a village to raise a child.
Children are certain cares but uncertain comforts.
What's bred in the bone will come out in the flesh.
Every mother thinks her own gosling a swan.
Children and fools speak the truth.
Small children, small worries; big children, big worries.
Every family has a skeleton in the cupboard.
A mother understands what a child does not say.
One father is more than a hundred schoolmasters.
It's a wise child that knows its own father.
As the twig is bent, so grows the tree.
An Englishman's home is his castle.
Home is where you hang your hat.
Fish and guests smell after three days.
There is always room for one more.
Every bird likes its own nest best.
It's an ill bird that fouls its own nest.
Men make houses, women make homes.
Home is home, be it ever so homely.
Dry bread at home is better than roast meat abroad.
It's the pot calling the kettle black.
Travel east or travel west, a man's own house is still the best.
The wider we roam, the welcomer home.
Go abroad and you'll hear news of home.
The proof of the pudding is in the eating.
Half a loaf is better than none.
One man's meat is another man's poison.
There's no use crying over spilt milk.
You can't make an omelette without breaking eggs.
The nearer the bone, the sweeter the meat.
Fine words butter no parsnips.
Breakfast like a king, lunch like a prince, dine like a pauper.
After dinner rest a while, after supper walk a mile.
There's many a slip 'twixt the cup and the lip.
You can have too much of a good thing.
Better an egg today than a hen tomorrow.
Every cook praises his own broth.
Too much pudding will choke a dog.
Eat at pleasure, drink by measure.
Better a small fish than an empty dish.
A cheerful look makes a dish a feast.
April showers bring May flowers.
One swallow does not make a summer.
Make hay while the sun shines.
The darkest hour is just before the dawn.
Ne'er cast a clout till May be out.
Red sky at night, shepherd's delight; red sky in the morning, shepherd's warning.
There is no rose without a thorn.
It's a long lane that has no turning.
You can't see the wood for the trees.
Everything is good in its season.
Oak before ash, in for a splash; ash before oak, in for a soak.
March comes in like a lion and goes out like a lamb.
There's no smoke without fire.
A rolling stone gathers no moss.
As the days lengthen, so the cold strengthens.
If you want to live and thrive, let the spider run alive.
The best things come in small packages.
You can't teach an old dog new tricks.
Curiosity killed the cat, but satisfaction brought it back.
When the cat's away, the mice will play.
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
A leopard cannot change its spots.
Don't change horses in midstream.
It's the last straw that breaks the camel's back.
You can't make a silk purse out of a sow's ear.
Don't put the cart before the horse.
Never look a gift horse in the mouth.
A cat in gloves catches no mice.
The cat would eat fish but would not wet her feet.
If you lie down with dogs, you will get up with fleas.
Every bird must hatch her own eggs.
It's an ill wind that blows nobody any good.
There is no such thing as bad weather, only the wrong clothes.
Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
After the storm comes the calm.
When the wind is in the east, 'tis neither good for man nor beast.
Mackerel sky, mackerel sky, never long wet and never long dry.
A sunshiny shower won't last half an hour.
When the dew is on the grass, rain will never come to pass.
Rain, rain, go away, come again another day.
The north wind doth blow, and we shall have snow.
Evening red and morning grey, two sure signs of one fine day.
When the swallows fly high, the weather will be dry.
Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise.
A good laugh and a long sleep are the best cures in the doctor's book.
Prevention is better than cure.
Feed a cold and starve a fever.
Health is not valued till sickness comes.
An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.
A good conscience is a soft pillow.
One hour's sleep before midnight is worth two after.
A creaking door hangs longest.
Sleep is better than medicine.
Cleanliness is next to godliness.
Don't burn the candle at both ends.
See a penny, pick it up, and all day long you'll have good luck.
It is better to be born lucky than rich.
Fortune knocks once at every man's door.
Break a mirror and you get seven years' bad luck.
When one door shuts, another opens.
A smooth sea never made a skilled sailor.
Laugh before breakfast, cry before supper.
A smile costs nothing but gives much.
Be happy while you're living, for you're a long time dead.
Count your blessings, not your troubles.
Worry often gives a small thing a big shadow.
Never cry before you are hurt.
Treat others as you would like to be treated.
One kind word can warm three winter months.
You catch more flies with honey than with vinegar.
Charity begins at home, but should not end there.
A little kindness goes a long way.
It takes two to make a quarrel.
What's sauce for the goose is sauce for the gander.
Beauty is only skin deep, but ugly goes to the bone.
The eyes are the window to the soul.
A good face is a letter of recommendation.
A fair face may hide a foul heart.
